description:
Found by Fable`s s503 review probes of s501q (`~/pcl-agent-scratch/s503/review/shadow2.pl` rows i, j; `r503q-levers.pl` row 27).  PRE-EXISTING: base 2284d58d and the s501q tree answer the same.

perl: `&name;` (no parens) calls name with the CURRENT @_ -- the very same array, so the callee`s `shift`, `pop`, `push @_, ...`, `@_ = ()` change the caller`s @_.  PCL emits `(pl-name @_)` (ir-spec.md, the `&foo;` rule): the callee gets the ELEMENTS (element aliasing works) but its own argument array, so structural changes are lost: `sub u1 { shift } sub u2 { &u1; scalar(@_) }` -> 3 (perl 2); `sub v1 { push @_, 9 } sub v2 { &v1; scalar(@_) }` -> 3 (perl 4).

Where it matters: the argument-parsing idiom `sub opts { &_parse_opts; ... }` and AUTOLOAD / wrapper trampolines that `shift` the invocant in a helper.  Census NOT taken: the cheap one is `grep -a -n -E "&[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9:]*;"` over lib/ + the CPAN board + perl`s lib, then reading which callees shift/pop/push.

Design note: s501q`s `_body_observes_args` predicate (one reading of "this body touches @_ itself": bare shift/pop, `&name;`, goto &sub) is the licence the raw-params levers ask; a fix here must keep `&name;` on the general path (it already counts as observing) and pass the caller`s argument VECTOR itself rather than its elements.  Check `goto &name` (which already carries @_ -- row 26 of the probe is right) for the mechanism to reuse.

Bar: the probe rows + guard rows; `cl/` + `Pl/` => gate, corpus-diff, sweep, companion op/sub.t op/goto.t comp/; bench rows fibret methret (the general call path must not slow).


=== DONE (s508a) ===
`&name;` / `&$code;` call with the caller's CURRENT @_, the same array: `(p-amp-call CALL)` binds *p-shared-args* and the callee's p-flatten-args adopts the vector on its ARRAY arm (a scalar-argument call never reads the special); a body's coalesced leading `my $x = shift;` run carries `(:shifts N)` and really shifts the shared vector (%p-shared-shift); `goto &g` from a frame whose @_ is a shared array hands it on shared.  A callee that only COPIES (p-raw-params, `:copy`) never asks.  Commits bbe60f65 + the shape rows in 0fe42517 (clform-01 43, codegen-01 111).  ir-spec §5 `&foo;` rule.  Guard transpile-test-10.t row 97 (fails on the base).  Sweep: op/aassign.t +1 row; companion op/aassign.t 181 -> 182, op/lex_assign.t 350 -> 351.
Census (callers whose callee changes @_'s shape): lib/ 4 sites / 0; CPAN board 43 sites / 11; perl's own lib 380 sites / 99 (158 callees outside the file).
FLAGGED, benched under the s509 stop rule (scratch/s508a/bench2632-clean.log, main c1d9bed7 extraction vs the tree, interleaved ABAB, K=5, load 1.2-1.3): fibret +3.0 % / +0.7 % against a main-vs-main band of 0.7 %; intloop+= -1.4/+1.0 (band 4.8), intloop= +3.8/-1.7 (band 3.8), subret -2.4/-1.1, methret -2.3/+1.9 (band 2.8), feargs +1.7/-2.5 (band 3.1), passarr -1.1/-0.8.  No row is more than 3 % beyond the band in both runs: shipped.

Companion (--all --quick, on b88a599a) and board (0 NEW / 0 FIXED / 0 LOST, 1827 = 1827) in the s508a session-log section; final bars there.
subject: `&name;` does not SHARE @_ with the callee (pre-existing): the callee`s `shift` / `push @_` are not seen by the caller -- `sub u1 { shift } sub u2 { &u1; scalar(@_) } u2(1,2,3)` answers 3, perl 2
